source.reading: chat_template.jinja lines 45-56: while enable_thinking is unset or true, reasoning_effort defaults to xhigh, any value other than xhigh, medium or low raises an error, and xhigh and low add an instruction to the system message. Lines 163-169: the generation prompt opens a <think> block, or an empty closed one when enable_thinking is false.

chat_template.jinja lines 2-3: reasoning_effort low or high selects that level, and any other value, or none, selects max; the level is written as a system line such as 'Reasoning Effort: Max'. Line 4: clear_thinking defaults to false, which keeps earlier turns' reasoning in the prompt. The last lines: the generation prompt always opens a <think> block, and no variable closes it. The two templates differ only in content and tool-call rendering.

chat_template.jinja lines 90-95: the generation prompt adds an empty closed <think></think> block when enable_thinking is false and leaves the reply open otherwise, so the model starts its own <think> block. The template reads no effort variable.

The checkpoint has no chat template; vLLM selects its deepseek_v41 tokenizer for DeepseekV41ForCausalLM, and the deepseek_v4 renderer passes every chat template argument to it unfiltered. deepseek_v41.py apply_chat_template: thinking is on unless the thinking or enable_thinking argument is false, or reasoning_effort is none; reasoning_effort defaults to high and must be low, high, xhigh, max or an integer from 1 to 100; drop_thinking defaults to true, which drops earlier turns' reasoning. deepseek_v41_encoding.py REASONING_EFFORT_MAPPINGS: low 50, high 75, xhigh 75, max 100, written as 'Reasoning Effort: N' at the start of the prompt.
